english_retrieval.title: Biography – All India Trinamool Congress
english_retrieval.snippet: Ms Mamata Banerjee, Hon’ble Chief Minister of West Bengal (15th, 16th and 17th Vidhan Sabha), and Chairperson, All India Trinamool Congress, daughter of Late Promileswar Banerjee and Mrs Gayatri Banerjee, was born in Kolkata. Her father was a freedom fighter and her mother who has supported her family through all its ups and downs, had instilled in Ms Banerjee the spirit of fair play, deep feeling for all human beings and the courage to stand for the downtrodden. In 1984, she was elected as a Member of Parliament from the Jadavpur Constituency and held the post of General Secretary of the Youth Congress (Indira) and became a member of the National Council in 1987 and a member of the Executive Committee of the Congress Parliamentary Party in 1988. She has served as a member of several Parliamentary Committees and was appointed as a Minister of State for Youth and Sports, Women and Child Development, Government of India in 1991.

english_retrieval.title: Mamata Banerjee: Latest News of Mamata Banerjee | Latest Updates, Photos & Videos
english_retrieval.snippet: # Mamata Banerjee. Mamata Banerjee is an Indian politician and the current Chief Minister of the state of West Bengal. She is the founder and current chairperson of the All India Trinamool Congress (AITC or TMC), a regional political party. Banerjee was born in Calcutta (now Kolkata), West Bengal in 1955. She began her political career as a member of the Indian National Congress party, but later left the party to form her own party, the TMC, in 1997. Banerjee has held various positions in government throughout her career, including serving as a Member of Parliament and a Member of the Legislative Assembly in West Bengal. In 2011, she led the TMC to a historic victory in the West Bengal assembly elections, ending the 34-year-long rule of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) in the state. She has been the Chief Minister of West Bengal since 2011 and has been re-elected in the 2016 and 2021 assembly elections. Madan Mitra has left *Mamata Banerjee*'s Trinamool Congress faction for a rebel group.

Mamata Banerjee Marks July 21 Martyrs' Day, Calls for United Democratic Resistance

West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee paid tribute to the martyrs of the July 21 movement and thanked TMC workers for the massive turnout in Kolkata. Addressing the Martyrs' Day rally, she called for democratic resistance against the BJP, accused it of divisive politics, and urged people to unite against violence and injustice.
